source: Instructor case: The Busy Med-Surg Shift — Patient 4
hpi: Linda was admitted yesterday evening with fever, productive cough, shortness of breath, and weakness. Chest X-ray demonstrated bilateral lower lobe infiltrates. She has a history of COPD and type 2 diabetes. She has been receiving IV antibiotics and supplemental oxygen. Overnight, nursing staff reported increasing fatigue and decreased oral intake.

handoff.situation: 63F admitted last evening with bilateral lower lobe CAP. On IV abx and 2 L NC.
handoff.background: COPD, T2DM, HTN, former smoker. NKDA. Full code.
handoff.assessment: Fatigued, febrile 101.3, HR 104, RR 24, BP 102/64, SpO2 91% on 2 L. Crackles bilateral bases. Decreased intake and urine output overnight. Lactate 2.8, WBC 17.8, Cr 1.4 (baseline 0.9).
handoff.recommendation: Watch closely for sepsis. Repeat lactate due. Strict I&O. COPD O2 target 88–92%.

baseline: Crackles in bilateral lower lung fields

findings: Urine output 15 mL over the last hour

labs.label: Repeat lactate
labs.notes: Value drafted; case only says repeat in 2–4 hours.

orders.text: Vital signs every 4 hours and as needed
Oxygen via nasal cannula, titrate according to prescribed COPD oxygen target of 88–92%
Obtain blood cultures x2 if not already collected, preferably before additional antibiotic administration if this does not delay treatment
Repeat CBC and CMP in the morning
Notify provider for systolic BP below 90, increasing oxygen requirements, worsening mental status, or decreasing urine output
Evaluate for sepsis and escalate care as indicated
Lactated Ringer's 30 mL/kg IV bolus now
Insert indwelling urinary catheter for hourly urine output

shouldRecognize: This patient is deteriorating and may be developing septic shock.
Immediate reassessment and escalation are needed.
Activate rapid response according to facility policy.
Assess airway, breathing, circulation, mental status, and perfusion.
Anticipate additional orders, including fluid resuscitation, repeat lactate, and possible higher-level care.
Review the patient's respiratory status and COPD oxygen target while responding to hypoxemia.
Monitor urine output and renal function.
